hypothesis: A loader-bound, flat-only transition contract with a verified active implementation baseline can move the shared live cohort to the evidence-routed v9 profile without profile ambiguity, hot mutation, or loss of rollback evidence.
decision: Freeze the evidence-routed v9 runbook and active implementation baseline. Do not alter the armed staged profile, stop the backend while HYPE is open, or start v9 automatically. At a fresh venue-flat and order-free boundary, stop the legacy backend, publish a candidate-bound report-only checkpoint, verify the exact v9 fingerprint, and use the unified explicitly armed launcher with its mandatory fresh pre-start backup.
falsifier: Any candidate file or loader fingerprint mismatch, changed or missing runbook or backup evidence, open venue position or order at transition, nonzero fault, concurrent checkpoint writer, missing fresh pre-start implementation identity, or first-position protection mismatch invalidates transition readiness.
limitations: The baseline proves profile and implementation bytes, not an atomic venue-state snapshot.
The current legacy process cannot withhold entries during its flat-to-STOP interval, so that one-time cutover retains an explicit entry race.
A new live start must create and independently verify a fresh mandatory pre-start bundle.
Transition correctness does not establish strategy profitability or durable edge.
The candidate remains inactive and the current open HYPE lifecycle remains governed by its original bound plan.
